text.p: Denmark's Phoenix roadbuilder's board on Friday said it recommended its shareholders to accept the bid for the firm of Norwegian Rieber & Son.

"The Phoenix Contractors board has been in contact with its advisers and assessed the bids for the company and can recommend shareholders to accept the bid from Rieber & Son ASA," Phoenix said in a statement.
"With this recommendation the board judges that the sale can go through, with shareholders securing the highest possible price for their Phoenix shares," it said.
On Thursday, Denmark's Icopal said it upheld its last 876 million crown bid for the local roadbuilder and would not raise its offer.
The move followed the raising last Friday by Norway's Rieber & Son of an earlier bid to 876 million crowns to match Icopal's rival offer.
After Thursday's Icopal announcement, Phoenix Board Chairman Henry Petersen told Reuters that it was going to recommend its shareholders to take the Rieber offer.
Both the Icopal and Rieber bids offer shareholders 790 crowns per share for A-shares in Phoenix Contractors and 710 crowns per share for C-shares.
Both bids expire on April 1 at 1500 GMT.
Thursday's statement from Icopal was the latest move in an increasingly bitter takeover struggle for Phoenix, launched by Rieber on January 15.

Heavyweight Danish construction and chemicals group Superfos, favoured by the pension funds which are Phoenix's largest shareholders, later made a higher bid but said it would not increase it again after Rieber leapfrogged ahead.
At one stage a fourth suitor for Phoenix, provincial Danish building contractor Marius Pedersen made an offer, but it expired two weeks ago.
The Phoenix board has earlier indicated its preference for Rieber on the grounds that the Norwegian firm seems more willing to respect the Jutland-based firm's autonomy and preserve jobs.
Rieber has a 25.7 percent equity stake in Phoenix with 23.1 percent of voting stock.

The scrabble for Phoenix is the first open takeover bidding in Denmark, where acquisitions have traditionally been announced only after they have been agreed in the boardroom and there is no real raider or hostile takeover culture. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
